title: Developer Experience in the Age of AI Coding Agents – Max Kanat-Alexander, Capital One
talk_summary: The talk argues that AI coding agents amplify existing developer-experience problems, so companies should invest in no-regrets fundamentals: standard tooling, fast deterministic validation, testable/structured code, written external context, and faster/higher-quality code review. Its core claim is that what is good for human developers is also good for agents, and weak review/validation creates a vicious cycle of rubber-stamped PRs and declining productivity.

takeaways.what_they_do: Make linters and tests runnable locally in seconds with clear, actionable errors so agents can iterate repeatedly without waiting on slow CI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any kind of objective deterministic validation that you give an agent will increase its capabilities

takeaways.technique: Assigned review routing with SLOs and turn state
takeaways.what_they_do: Assign PRs to specific reviewers and enforce SLOs, making it unambiguous whose turn it is instead of broadcasting review requests to a channel.

takeaways.technique: High review bar to avoid rubber-stamping
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a review process capable of rejecting bad changes; otherwise more agent PRs lead to rubber-stamp approvals and a harder-to-maintain codebase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you don't have a process that is capable of rejecting things that shouldn't go in

takeaways.technique: Write down external context and intent
takeaways.what_they_do: Document requirements, why decisions were made, and external data shapes that cannot be inferred from code so agents do not rely on tribal knowledge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anything that can't be in the code or isn't in the code needs to somehow be written somewhere that the agent can access

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose actions as CLIs or APIs with text output instead of making agents drive browsers or computer-use interfaces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agents need either a CLI or an API to take that action

takeaways.technique: Standardize dev environment to training-set norms
takeaways.what_they_do: Use common package managers, linters, languages, and commands the same way the outside world does; avoid bespoke tooling that fights the model's training data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use the industry standard tools in the same way the industry uses them
